question: r-selected species have maximum:
solution:
The correct answer is __**reproductive rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **r-selected species** are characterized by high reproductive rates. They produce a large number of offspring in a relatively short period.

• These species usually inhabit **unstable or unpredictable environments** where the probability of offspring survival is low.

• Due to their high reproductive rates, **r-selected species** can quickly exploit available resources and reproduce rapidly.

• Examples of r-selected species include many **insects, small rodents, and annual plants**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Mortality rate:**

• This refers to the number of deaths in a population over a period. In r-selected species, the mortality rate of offspring is typically high due to less parental care and harsh environmental conditions.

• **Survival rate:**

• This is the proportion of individuals surviving to a certain age. In r-selected species, the survival rate is generally low because many offspring do not reach maturity.

• **Parental care:**

• This refers to the care provided by parents to their offspring. r-selected species often exhibit minimal or no parental care, focusing instead on producing many offspring.

• **K-selected species:**

• In contrast to r-selected species, K-selected species have lower reproductive rates, produce fewer offspring, and provide significant parental care. They are adapted to stable environments where competition for resources is high.

• Examples of K-selected species include large mammals like elephants and whales, as well as some birds and trees.
